anomalies.observed: The two alternative MCU footprints map POT and TACH to opposite physical pins: on U2 (ATtiny45-20P, THT) pin 2 = POT and pin 3 = TACH, while on U3 (ATtiny13V-10S, SMD) pin 3 = POT and pin 2 = TACH. All other pins (5=SDA, 6=PWM, 7=SCK, 1=RST, 8=VCC, 4=GND) agree.
anomalies.expected: U2 and U3 are the THT and SMD alternatives for the same 8-pin ATtiny (same PB0-PB5 layout), so they must be drop-in equivalent: each external signal has to land on the same physical pin in both footprints so a single firmware pin-assignment works for either build.

evidence.quote: U2 ATtiny45-20P: '2 POT', '3 TACH' (right page, sheet /, fan_controller.kicad_sch)
U3 ATtiny13V-10S: '3 POT', '2 TACH' (right page, sheet /, fan_controller.kicad_sch)

anomalies.impact: A board assembled with the SMD footprint (U3) would tie the potentiometer wiper to the pin the firmware treats as the tachometer input and the tach signal to the pin it treats as the analog pot input, so the closed-loop fan-speed control reads the wrong signals and fails to regulate.

parsed.summary: The drawing shows the THT (U2) and SMD (U3) alternative ATtiny footprints with POT and TACH swapped between physical pins 2 and 3, which breaks drop-in compatibility and would mis-wire the speed-control loop on a board built with the SMD part; this is the one deviation supported by the schematic.
